chunks: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr, from al-Qunbari - from the descendants of Qambar al-Kabir - the mawla of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

The narration of Ja'far was mentioned, so he cursed him. I said: Have you seen him? He replied: I did not see him, but someone else saw him. I said: And who is that? He replied: Ja'far saw him twice, and he has a narration.

key_terms.جَعْفَرُ: Ja'far ibn Muhammad (often referred to as Ja'far al-Sadiq or his son depending on context, here likely the one who saw the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who saw the Imam of the Age during the Minor Occultation according to al-Qunbari?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the chain of transmission regarding the sighting of Imam al-Mahdi by Ja'far ibn Muhammad, a key figure in the Minor Occultation (*al-Ghayb al-Sughra*). It underscores the scholarly reliance on eyewitness accounts to validate the Imam's continued presence among the people, even if not all scholars personally witnessed him. The mention of Ja'far having a specific hadith further establishes his authority as a reliable witness in the context of the Occultation.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 217 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Yaqub from Ahmad bin Nadhr that he asked Qambari, a descendant of Qambar senior, servant of Imam Ali Ridha (a.s):

The incident of Ja’far, the liar was mentioned. Qambari scolded him and spoke against it. I asked: No one other than him is eligible for Imamate; have you seen someone else [Master of the Age (a.s)]? He replied: Not me, but someone else has. I asked: Who is that? He replied: Ja’far, and he saw him twice, and he is aware of it.
